After the high flat top passes, P must follow the sloping front down through zero to the narrow negative dip, then jump back to zero.
walkthrough: Fix attention on particle P at $s=0$ on the right while the whole pulse shape moves right toward it without changing shape.
The first part to arrive is the leading vertical edge, where the rope to the left is high and the rope at P is at zero, so $s$ jumps suddenly from $0$ to a positive value.
Next the horizontal high top passes P, so $s$ stays constant and positive for a time interval.
Then the sloping rising front in the space diagram passes P from right to left, so at fixed P the displacement falls steadily from positive through zero to negative.
Finally the narrow negative dip passes and the trailing vertical edge returns the rope to zero, so $s$ jumps suddenly from negative back to $0$ and stays there.
